question:
In the process of bisecting angle BAC in the given figure, why do we draw arcs from points D and E?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7cce169ccaea2f3897924f6c624f4a5bc784af8f93e1ad6e808a07fb71c33f7e.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __To intersect above A__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To bisect angle BAC__, it is crucial to draw arcs from points D and E.
 
• This ensures that the arcs intersect above the vertex A, helping to locate the point for the angle bisector.
 
• The intersection point of the arcs guides the accurate drawing of the angle bisector.
 
• Without this step, the angle bisector cannot be drawn precisely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Steps to Bisect an Angle:**

 
 
• Place the compass at the vertex of the angle and draw an arc intersecting both arms of the angle.
 
• Mark the intersection points as D and E.
 
• From points D and E, draw arcs intersecting above the vertex.
 
• Draw a straight line from the vertex through the intersection point of the arcs to bisect the angle.
